chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who touched his wife's private part. He said: There is nothing upon him; and if he wishes, he may wash his hand. And because of a kiss, wudu (ablution) is not required.

key_terms.لَا يُتَوَضَّأُ مِنْهَا: wudu (ablution) is not required because of it
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no legal consequence upon him here

ai.seo_question: Does touching one's wife or kissing invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that touching one's wife's private part does not itself necessitate wudu (ablution). It also states that kissing does not invalidate wudu (ablution), though washing the hand is permitted if one wishes.
